note: Used before a noun (別的東西 bié de dōng xi 'other things') or on its own (還要別的嗎？ 'anything else?'). 'Other people' is usually 別人 bié rén; 其他 qí tā is a bit more formal.
Usually comes as 試試看 shì shi kàn or 試一下 shì yī xià ('give it a try'), or 試穿 shì chuān 'try on clothes'.

example.english: You can give it a try.

gloss: to belong to; to fall under
note: Used for categories, scope or responsibility. For simple ownership people say 是他的 shì tā de 'it's his'.

example.trad: 這不屬於我的工作範圍。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù shǔyú wǒ de gōngzuò fànwéi.
example.english: This isn't part of my job.

note: In everyday Taiwan speech 房間 usually means a bedroom: 回房間 'go to my room'.
A location word, used after a noun: 桌子上面 'on the table'. MOE lists shàng mian with a neutral tone, but Taiwanese usually say shàng miàn.

example.english: The phone is on the table.

note: Formal or written. In everyday Taiwan speech 老公 lǎo gōng is far more common. Taiwan (MOE) says zhàng fū; the mainland says zhàng fu.

hint: inner or collective power, not lì qi
note: MOE gives lì liang; many Taiwanese say lì liàng. Physical strength (as in having no energy left) is usually 力氣 lì qi.

example.trad: 你的話給了我很多力量。
example.pinyin: Nǐ de huà gěi le wǒ hěn duō lìliang.
example.english: Your words gave me a lot of strength.

hint: at the end of a sentence
note: Goes at the end of a sentence to play something down, often together with 只是 or 只有: 只是開玩笑而已 'just joking, that's all'.

hint: both directions, depending on word order
note: 跟…借 gēn … jiè 'borrow from…': 我跟他借錢 'I borrowed money from him'. 借…給 or 借 + person means 'lend': 借我 'lend me'. To give it back is 還 huán.

example.pinyin: Kěyǐ jiè wǒ yī zhī bǐ ma?
example.english: Could you lend me a pen?

note: Often said as 猜猜看 cāi cai kàn 'take a guess'.
Measure word for episodes of TV shows and series: 這部連續劇有二十集 zhè bù lián xù jù yǒu èr shí jí 'this series has twenty episodes'. Also means 'to gather', mostly inside words like 集合 jí hé.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān kàn le sān jí.

note: Used to answer the phone or to call out to someone. MOE gives wèi; mainland dictionaries give wéi for the phone greeting, and in real speech it often comes out rising. As a verb, wèi means 'to feed' (喂奶 wèi nǎi).

example.english: Hello? Who would you like to speak to?

note: Picks out part of a group, often in pairs: 有的人…，有的人… 'some people ..., others ...'.

example.trad: 有的人喜歡，有的人不喜歡。
example.pinyin: Yǒude rén xǐhuān, yǒude rén bù xǐhuān.
example.english: Some people like it, some don't.

note: Mostly heard inside words: 前面 qián miàn, 見面 jiàn miàn 'to meet'; a person's face is 臉 liǎn. Also a measure word for flat things (一面鏡子 yī miàn jìng zi 'a mirror'). 'Noodles' (麵) sounds the same.
Sounds the same as 面 'side / surface'. Common in Taiwan food: 牛肉麵 niú ròu miàn 'beef noodle soup', 炒麵 chǎo miàn 'fried noodles'.

example.english: I want to eat beef noodle soup.

note: Implies that the plan or situation later changed: 我本來要去，可是… 'I was going to go, but ...'.

example.trad: 我本來想去，後來太累了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ běnlái xiǎng qù, hòulái tài lèi le.
example.english: I wanted to go at first, but then I got too tired.

example.pinyin: Tā bù chéngrèn shì tā zuò de.
example.english: He won't admit he did it.

note: 慢一點 màn yī diǎn 'a bit slower'. 慢慢來 màn màn lái 'take your time'. 慢走 màn zǒu 'take care' is said to a guest who is leaving.

example.english: Take your time, there's no rush.

note: Used both for people stating something and for things that indicate or mean something: 這表示… 'this means ...'.

example.trad: 他沒回答，表示他不同意。
example.pinyin: Tā méi huídá, biǎoshì tā bù tóngyì.
example.english: He didn't answer, which means he disagrees.

note: 沒想到 méi xiǎng dào means 'didn't expect' or 'surprisingly'.

example.pinyin: Wǒ méi xiǎngdào nǐ huì lái.
example.english: I didn't expect you to come.

note: The noun. 'To have a meeting' is usually 開會 kāi huì.

example.english: What time does the meeting start?

note: Counted with 首 shǒu: 一首歌. 'To sing' is 唱歌 chàng gē.
Measure word for drinks: 一杯水 yī bēi shuǐ 'a glass of water', 兩杯咖啡. The cup itself is 杯子 bēi zi.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yào yī bēi rè chá.
example.english: I'd like a cup of hot tea.

note: The general word for alcoholic drinks. Specific kinds: 啤酒 pí jiǔ 'beer', 紅酒 hóng jiǔ 'red wine'. 喝酒 hē jiǔ means 'to drink (alcohol)'.

example.pinyin: Tā wǎnshang hē le hěn duō jiǔ.
example.english: He drank a lot this evening.

note: Body part + 痛: 頭痛 tóu tòng 'headache', 肚子痛 dù zi tòng 'stomachache'. 好痛！ hǎo tòng 'ouch!'. 痛苦 tòng kǔ is deeper, longer suffering.
Also means 'my family': 家裡有四個人. MOE lists jiā li with a neutral tone, but Taiwanese usually say jiā lǐ.
Often before a noun with 的: 同樣的問題 'the same problem'. In casual speech 一樣 yī yàng is more common.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yě yǒu tóngyàng de wèntí.

note: The Christian God is usually 上帝 shàng dì. Also used in slang: 好神 hǎo shén or 太神了 'amazing / uncanny'.
The everyday word for morning; 上午 shàng wǔ is more formal, like 'a.m.' in schedules. MOE gives zǎo shang; many Taiwanese say zǎo shàng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: I get up at seven every morning.

note: Usually paired with 也 yě in the second clause: 即使下雨，我也要去 'even if it rains, I'll still go'. 就算 jiù suàn is the more casual equivalent.

example.pinyin: Jíshǐ hěn lèi, tā yě qù shàngbān.
example.english: Even when he's tired, he still goes to work.

hint: what happened next, in the past
note: Only for past events ('and then later ...'). For the future, use 以後 yǐ hòu or 等一下 děng yī xià.
For answering a question. Replying to a message is usually 回 huí (回訊息 'reply to a message').

example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu huídá wǒ de wèntí.

note: 有意見 yǒu yì jiàn can also mean 'to have an objection or complaint', so 你有什麼意見？ can sound like 'Got a problem with that?'

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tīngting nǐ de yìjiàn.
example.english: I'd like to hear your opinion.

gloss: to care about; to be concerned
to leave behind; to stay behind
note: MOE lists liú xia with a light 下, but the full tone is common in Taiwan speech. 留下來 liú xià lái means 'to stay (on)'.

example.pinyin: Tā liúxià yī fēng xìn jiù zǒu le.
example.english: He left a letter and went away.

note: Praise for skill: 你好厲害 nǐ hǎo lì hài 'you're amazing!'. Also 'severe, intense': 痛得很厲害 tòng de hěn lì hài 'it hurts badly'. MOE gives full tones (lì hài); the mainland says lì hai.

hint: a bit more formal than cháng cháng
note: Everyday speech often uses 常常 cháng cháng or just 常 cháng.

gloss: no need to; don't have to
note: Spoken bú yòng (不 becomes bú before a 4th tone). Also a polite reply: 不用了 'no thanks', 不用謝 bù yòng xiè 'no need to thank me'.

example.english: You don't need to wait for me.

note: Before a verb it can mean 'hard to': 不好找 'hard to find'. 不好意思 bù hǎo yì si means 'sorry / excuse me'.

gloss: to pretend; to pack in; to install
hint: fake it, or put something in
note: Covers 'pretend' (別裝了 bié zhuāng le 'stop pretending'), 'put into a container' (裝水) and 'install' (裝冷氣 'install an air conditioner').

example.pinyin: Bié zhuāng le, wǒ zhīdào shì nǐ.
example.english: Stop pretending, I know it was you.

hint: to open a list of points
note: Starts a sequence of points, often followed by 然後 or 再來. Compare 先 xiān 'do first, beforehand'.

example.english: First of all, you need to be patient.

note: 年輕人 nián qīng rén means 'young people'.
Most often used when you realize something: 原來如此 yuán lái rú cǐ 'I see'. Also 'original, former': 原來的地方 'the original place'.

example.english: My parents are against us getting married.

gloss: no way; not OK; not allowed
note: The opposite of 行 xíng 'OK'. Also 'no good at' (我數學不行 'I'm bad at math') and, after an adjective, 'extremely' (累得不行 'exhausted').
The opposite is 髒 zāng 'dirty'. 乾 here is gān 'dry', not qián. MOE gives full tones (gān jìng); the mainland says gān jing.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ fángjiān dǎsǎo gānjìng le.
